What if the whole world dropped to minus 100 degrees Celsius?
Exposed skin freezes in seconds. Hypothermia sets in within minutes.
Pipes burst, and lakes freeze solid.
Batteries die. Phones and computers shut down.
Oil turns thick, diesel gels, and tires turn brittle.
Power lines snap, and cities go dark.
Concrete and steel crack, and buildings get damaged.
Plants die, and farming comes to an end.
Your breath turns into ice crystals the moment you exhale.
The coldest ever recorded is minus 89 degrees, in Antarctica. Minus 100? Never measured. Follow for more.
